content:
The image shows a longitudinal cross-section of a corn stalk/cob interior. Key features:
- Orange-brown discolored pith tissue
- Numerous small black dots scattered throughout the tissue — these are fungal pycnidia (fruiting bodies)
- Corn kernels visible at the top (honeycomb pattern)
- The tissue breakdown is internal, affecting the stalk pith

The scattered black pycnidia embedded in brown/orange discolored stalk pith is the hallmark of **Diplodia stalk rot** (*Stenocarpella maydis*). The orange-brown internal coloration and dense distribution of small black pycnidia match this disease precisely. Charcoal rot would show grayish-black sclerotia; Anthracnose stalk rot would show external shiny black lesions; Fusarium would show pink/salmon discoloration.
